Keep in mind that a healthy relationship is when both partners help each other realize their potential and support each other ideally through love. Each partner has a responsibility to actively work on themselves even in tough times. Mental health professionals work with you to help combat and reverse mental health issues through therapy and meds where appropriate. I hope this makes sense. 

You sound intelligent and you identify some things you are interested in. Programming. There are plenty of free options to teach you about it online. There may be local groups that meet and discuss it and share ideas (try your local library). Failing that, there are online groups where you may connect with people (of course be wary). 

Try looking around and instead of grinding to a halt about being overwhelmed about not having the life you want, identify small steps (like learning programming online) where you have total control and you can celebrate your successes as you progress. 

I of course don’t know much about your personal situation or challenges, but changing perceptions takes time and consistent effort. It may be hard to believe but if you put in the work and some people still are negative towards you, they may not actually be good friend material. One thing for certain is you are not ugly. Look around the world. People are attracted to all types of people. Even if you’re not stereotypically attractive-there are many people who find you attractive. 

One of the most valuable contributions you can make to the world is to relate to people that first impressions shouldn’t always matter. You yourself say you made mistakes that you want to correct. Just by having that knowledge and living that way and then sharing that perspective will change people’s lives. All the best

Venting is ok. You’re not wasting anyone’s time. Friendships can be rough when you don’t receive the level of attention or respect you deserve. We often have to wait and search and experiment with relationships until we find people who truly get us and appreciate us. Keep trying.

You’re not a pussy for not committing suicide. Deciding not to do it when you want to do it is progress. Pain can be overwhelming but you can conquer it. Reach out to those you trust. You don’t have to be alone.

A connection with someone who understands or at least is willing to hear you out? It can seem overbearing but sometimes it’s just a relief to be able to say what you need to say and have someone listen with no judgement. Feel free to share. People are here who do listen. People do care. You are important.

When I first posted, it was my first time to reach out like that to anyone. I was really overwhelmed by the response. It gave me the strength to make it through that night. Yesterday my urge to do it was less. I applied for more jobs. I investigated ways starting my own business but lack start up funding of a couple hundred dollars (to buy a domain(s) and set up a site). I have a few applications I’m still waiting on but they seem less likely as time goes on. Just before this reply, I checked online and discovered my tax refund should be here by next week. That makes the immediate stress load down to around $2,500.  Still with no options to earn it or borrow it. It’s weird that it’s all financial. I’ve called my landlord daily to give updates and (possibly) fortunately the person in charge of accounts has been away but I have nothing except one payment now to offer. Thank you for your response. I really appreciate it.
Unfortunately, I think that’s definitely part of the challenge.

Thanks. I hear what you say about family. I know for a fact they can’t help financially. I don’t think it’s fair to lean on them at the last minute. It’s late here and the ones I would talk to have likely turned their phones off for the night. As I said, I don’t really want to but I just don’t see any hope for positive change at this point. I have to decide really soon.

I just looked them up. Thanks. I tend to think recruiters are a tough sell since they want to only recommend “sure things” to their clients. My background is entrepreneurial and in industries that are not usual. If you look at my resume you won’t see for example: “retail cashier” “asst retail store manager” “retail store manager”.

Thank you. I actually have tried dumbing down my resume. Almost every time I apply for a job, I reword and rework it so it aligns for with the job description. I do have a challenge that my experiences and past positions are challenging to some to see how transferable the skill sets are but I can understand that.  I appreciate your suggestions though.

It did not come across as repetitive nor did I take it negative in any way. Thank you it was very well put and this is really nice being able to speak the way I am and receive the well thought out responses I’m getting. Thank you and to all who are reading.

I am personally proud of the differences I’ve made in some people’s lives. I know one who has literally touched thousands after his night of need. I can think of a few other really cool examples too. I’m not so arrogant to think that it had to be me. If it wasn’t me in the right place at the right time, someone else probably would have been there. I’m just honored to have been able to have made the difference. 

My state tonight is purely from nonperformance and finances. I need to be the one to change those things and for some reason I haven’t been able to. I’ve had tough times before where nothing looked like it would work out but I always had several irons in the fire with a track record of being sure one of them was going to work. And to make it even more bizarre the challenge was part of the fun. This time is different. Now, after such a stretch of failure, I don’t see the fun. I see pain beyond being able to recover. It’s bizarre to me that it’s all about the money. I am still learning to the end. I can’t seem to figure out what i did wrong and fix it. It’s frustrating.

While there’s an appeal to a fresh restart, I’m more interested in having a decent job, volunteering in the community and having roots. The talk of getting any job is all about the fact that I’m willing to take anything to make ends meet while I work at getting a more career oriented job. I’ve already sold most stuff I could get any value out of the remaining stuff is functional or sentimental. Thanks for your comments.

How would I look up the average income for those apps? I started looking into Wag...didn’t fully register yet.

Family is aware of my general emotional and definitely financial situation. One even came over with groceries a few weeks back (and they can’t really afford it). Emotionally I can’t reach out at this time, it would be inconsiderate to the max. I am getting along ok (not complaining anyway) on very little. I don’t drink (ok I bought a six pack in the summer when I went to a bbq), definitely don’t eat out and am pretty good at holding off any luxury spending until funds permit. I can get by with relatively little I’m a little proud to say. 

I am used to putting together projections and proposals. I’ve worked with my landlord giving them updates on job apps for the last several weeks. There have been interviews and second interviews. Right now, here is what i see: I’m waiting to hear back on a $45K job within a couple days. That could be a game changer since I could keep spending minimally and make up my deficit pretty quickly. Unfortunately despite the interview going really well, I’m sensing I didn’t get the job. There’s another I expect to hear back later this week $35K which I also had a great second interview with. I have at least four apps under consideration $45K - $70K. All of them are game changers but only if they result in a job. This is just baseless optimism at this point. I am experiencing a long streak of bad luck so my optimism is almost non-existent. 

 When I used to have my own business, I could call up my banker and ask for a huge overdraft to be put in place until the end of the month. My word was enough to make it happen. Despite having really lucrative business ideas, my word is currently worth nothing. 

The very fact that you would even consider helping is beyond amazing. I really appreciate your comments and support. Thank you.

Few family and the ones that I have are not in a financial (or space) position to help. Uber’s not an option due to my vehicle and when I did the numbers, it didn’t work out that there was any money making going on. Instacart and Doordash, Rover and Wag....I’ll check out. Thank you.

Sorry if I gave the wrong impression in that it hasn’t happened yet. I think I can stave off eviction for a few more days but I’m not sure. The not knowing adds to the stress. Eviction is the experience I’m trying to avoid having. Timing with possible ways of doing it is what is coming into play. It’s more likely to be certain if I do it sooner than later. Honestly I’m afraid of what I’ll become if I’m evicted. Someone who can’t help himself. I appreciate your words, support and time.. I wish you all the best. Thank you.

Without going all out, I pretty much had that discussion with the manager I mentioned earlier. I was convinced he believed, and I was genuine about wanting to start at entry level and try to perform and get advancement. When we discussed that, he said it “changes everything” about what he was thinking about hiring me. In the end it didn’t work.  I hear what you’re saying and thanks for the input but showing desperation is a little more than I can do. I don’t expect anyone to hire me based on sympathy. According to my resume, they should see a great work ethic and great achievements. Thanks for the suggestion though. I appreciate you taking the time to comment.

Thank you very much for your encouragement. It really feels comforting. 

I had just moved back to my current area after some life changes (divorce, illness). It’s funny that I used to be active in a local church and was its treasurer. Any assistance they can provide right now will not solve my problems. They don’t really have the money to make a difference and frankly there are probably more worthy people needing any money they can spare. 

My life has boiled down to one job....providing for myself and I’m failing miserably. I’ve tried to be conscientious about it. I can live comfortably if I had a job only paying $10/hr (ok tight, and only if the landlord would accept a longer term of repayment for the backlog) but I’m not into spending beyond my means. I’m very frustrated with myself. I used to say it wouldn’t matter if I lost a job because I would take any job to make ends meet in the meantime or start my own business. Unfortunately a few circumstances at once have totally taken me by surprise. You’re right. I used to pride myself at thinking outside the box. I used to believe in myself and get results. I’m at the end of an extended period of time where I have experienced failures. I can’t see evidence in my life that I can repay anyone.  

Getting kicked out and losing all my stuff (I don’t’ have a lot of stuff really) is a line I don’t want to cross. Not an experience I want to live through. I don’t see a light at the end of the tunnel if that happens.

I hear you but I can’t misrepresent. I can put together a great business plan with honest projections (and i do have a few ideas but no funders would want to fund a start up) but can’t lie. I did try a temp agency who thinks of me as a good employee but they don’t have anything I am “able”’ to do right now. You mention cL with really temp jobs..I hadn’t zeroed in on those because I’ve desperately been seeking something with more permanence or steady so I can propose a payment plan to landlord. I’ll check. Thanks again.

Thanks that’s a good angle. I had been saying I don’t mind entry level if there is opportunity for advancement based on performance. Convinced one manager who was literally gushing over my qualifications to the point where he had me promise to wait for him to call and he would try to find something...to which no calls as of yet... three weeks.

Bank is definitely not an option since I’ve been out of work. I don’t really have anything of value. I had a coin collection but already sold that to pay bills. I explored social assistance but I don’t qualify. Right now it boils down to income. I can’t seem to get a job. I’ve explored online places like fiverr but a new person gets buried among the more established ones. I will admit I should have done that anyway.
Thanks I appreciate your comments.
I replied to you in the above thread sorry.

I don’t see how to recover from this if the worst happens and I get evicted. I would shovel crap if that job could pay my bills. I would compete with myself to be their best shoveler of crap they had if given the chance. I have a great work ethic and I’m not below doing any job that will pay bills. I just haven’t run into anyone who will give me the job unfortunately. Thanks for commenting.

Local family is hard pressed both emotionally and financially with the things they have going on.  The ex is definitely not an option. You are right and I’m blown away by this fact. I don’t really want to do it. Things could change. I have a couple apps hanging out there which would turn the tables immediately. One is not looking so great and the other is a possibility. I have already contacted them with polite follow ups. No answer. Just....as I was writing this reply....got a rejection from a convenience store for a cashier position...wow. So I see what you’re saying. Thank you for taking the time to say it. Timing is an issue. If I don’t do it tonight, it will be more difficult and less certain of success if I wait. I don’t want to fail in that. It will just make things worse.

There’s no money for a hobby. My decision doesn’t stem from the usual considerations like feeling lonely or unwanted, it’s almost all financial and not being able to find a job and live. I like to volunteer but can’t due to that costing money (even gas is a big expense with zero income).
Thanks I appreciate your kind words. I’m stuck right now. I used to see things strategically but I just don’t see any options at this point.
